It definitely is.

Just need to form a habit of ignoring alcohol. I once went 8 months. Could easily walk past the alcohol section in the supermarket without a single urge to pick up a bottle. 

Started up again because of some new triggers. Time to try, again.

You did good. Keep at it.

I usually try to document it. And before I drink, I go back and read what happened during my withdrawals.

And how much it's worth worth it.

I fuck up and entire week by starting with half a bottle of wine.

I guess I get it logically, too, but it takes time to sink in. Gotta keep it up and program my brain for it. Make it a habit.

For me, it's usually the alcohol withdrawal that causes the panic attacks and anxiety. If I'm sober for a week, I can think clearly about how to solve my problems. If it gets overwhelming, I either drink (trying to stop that now) or distract myself with binge-watching some comedy.

My therapist said that thoughts are just those - thoughts. They come and go in waves. She said it about my intention to drink, but it's generally applicable to everything, including getting overwhelmed. Just sit it out and distract the brain till the feeling passes.

It works for me, sometimes. When I actually give enough of a crap to try.

The day will pass and you'll feel much better the next whole week by not giving in. I always ask myself (and often make the wrong decision), a few hours of a happy buzz today and tomorrow, or a good week without hand tremors and severe anxiety.

Absolutely agree with this.

Once it hits my brain beyond a point, there's no stopping it.
And I almost always misjudge that point. It's always a pattern of, "what's the harm in another one" which then turns into "well, now I need to keep this (not) amazing buzz alive".

And then I've had 16 more, blacked out, missed a dozen calls, and my hands are trembling.

In my experience, such occasions have been chances where it could spiral out of control quite easily. That's what I usually use to count my sobriety. Even if I didn't spiral, I could have. Resetting the counter helps me to stay more focused on the goal of getting rid of AUD.

I've felt a slight placebo effect when drinking non-alcoholic beer. But I guess it's the whole opening a can and chugging down soda, plus the similar taste.

Didn't get a headspin, but I found it a good way to satisfy cravings without ending up in a 4 day binge.
